blocks.title: Operating System and Secure Protocol Configuration comparison
Operating System and Secure Protocol Configuration exam shortcuts
items: Need to push Windows security settings to many domain systems → GROUP POLICY
Use centralized policy rather than configuring every host manually.
Example: Enforce password and firewall settings across workstations.
Linux process should be restricted beyond standard permissions → SELINUX
Mandatory access controls can constrain process behavior.
Example: A web server process is prevented from reading unrelated files.
Insecure protocol is currently used → SELECT SECURE PROTOCOL
Replace legacy insecure protocols with secure alternatives.
Service must use approved secure port → PORT SELECTION
Ensure firewall and service configuration align with the chosen protocol.
Traffic needs protected transport → TRANSPORT METHOD
Choose encryption or tunneling appropriate to the connection.
Example: Use TLS for application traffic or IPsec for secure IP transport.
blocks.example: Focus on what needs to be changed: traffic rules, detection logic, protocol choice, filtering policy, endpoint response, or user-behavior controls.

questions.q: A company wants to centrally enforce Windows password and firewall settings across domain-joined computers. Which capability should be modified?
questions.explanation: Group Policy centrally enforces Windows configuration across domain systems.

questions.q: A Linux web-server process should be prevented from reading unrelated files even if normal permissions are misconfigured. Which control best fits?
questions.explanation: SELinux provides mandatory access control beyond standard discretionary permissions.

questions.q: An administrator replaces Telnet with SSH for remote management. Which implementation choice is being changed?
questions.explanation: The insecure protocol is being replaced with a secure protocol.

questions.q: A secure web service should listen on its standard HTTPS port. Which setting is being modified?
questions.explanation: Port selection determines the service port used by the protocol.

questions.q: Two sites need protected IP-layer transport across an untrusted network. Which implementation consideration is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Transport method covers how traffic is carried or protected, such as with IPsec.
